question: The first modern Olympic Games was held in the year _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1896.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. (आधुनिक ओलंपिक — 1896, एथेंस)

 

• They were organised largely due to the efforts of Baron Pierre de Coubertin, the founder of the International Olympic Committee (IOC), which was established in 1894.

 

• A total of 14 nations and around 241 athletes competed in 43 events across 9 sports at these Games.

 

• The 1896 Games revived the ancient Olympic tradition of Greece and marked the beginning of the modern Olympic movement, held every four years since (with exceptions during the World Wars).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was founded in 1894 in Paris on the initiative of Pierre de Coubertin.

 

• India first participated in the Olympic Games in 1900 (Paris), represented by a single athlete, Norman Pritchard.

 

NOTE

 

• 1894 (Option 1): This is the year the IOC was founded, not the year the first modern Games were held.

 

• 1892 (Option 2): No Olympic Games were held in this year; Coubertin proposed reviving the Olympics around this period.

 

• 1900 (Option 4): The second modern Olympic Games were held in Paris in 1900, not the first.

question: In which month of the Islamic calendar is ‘Ramadan’,a holy time when Muslims around the world fast and focus their attention on giving to charity (known as Zakat), observed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ninth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic (Hijri) lunar calendar. (रमजान — नौवां महीना)

 

• It is observed by Muslims worldwide as a month of fasting (Sawm) from dawn to sunset, prayer, reflection, and community, and is one of the Five Pillars of Islam.

 

• During Ramadan, Muslims also focus on Zakat (charity), one of the Five Pillars, which involves giving a portion of one's wealth to those in need.

 

• The month concludes with the festival of Eid-ul-Fitr, which marks the end of the fasting period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Five Pillars of Islam are: Shahada (faith), Salat (prayer), Zakat (charity), Sawm (fasting during Ramadan), and Hajj (pilgrimage to Mecca).

 

• The Islamic calendar is a lunar calendar of 12 months, so Ramadan shifts earlier by about 10-11 days each year relative to the Gregorian calendar.

 

NOTE

 

• Second (Option 2): The second month of the Islamic calendar is Safar, not associated with fasting.

 

• Seventh (Option 3): The seventh month is Rajab, one of the four sacred months in Islam, but not the fasting month.

 

• Sixth (Option 4): The sixth month is Jumada al-Thani, unrelated to Ramadan.

question: Radhe Sham Barle received the Padma Shri in 2020-21 for promoting the Panthi dance of tribals from the Santnami community on the birth anniversary of Guru Ghasidas. Which state does this dance form belong to?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Radheshyam Barle was conferred the Padma Shri in 2021 for his contribution to promoting the Panthi dance of Chhattisgarh. (पंथी नृत्य — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• Panthi dance is a traditional folk dance of the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh, performed to celebrate the birth anniversary of Guru Ghasidas, the founder of the Satnami sect.

 

• The dance is performed with rhythmic movements and acrobatic feats, accompanied by devotional songs (panthi geet) glorifying Guru Ghasidas's teachings of equality and social reform.

 

• Guru Ghasidas Jayanti is celebrated on 18 December and is an important occasion for the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important folk dances of Chhattisgarh include Raut Nacha, Karma, and Saila.

 

• The Satnami community, founded by Guru Ghasidas in the early 19th century, propagated the worship of one formless God (Satnam) and opposed caste discrimination.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha (Options 1, 3, 4): Panthi dance is not native to these states; it is specifically associated with the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh.

question: Padma Shri awardee, Darshana Jhaveri is a __________ dancer of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Darshana Jhaveri is a renowned Manipuri classical dancer of India, honoured with the Padma Shri. (दर्शना झावेरी — मणिपुरी नृत्य)

 

• She, along with her sisters (the Jhaveri Sisters), played a pivotal role in bringing Manipuri dance from Manipur to mainstream national and international recognition.

 

• She trained under gurus in Manipur and has spent decades researching, documenting, and teaching the Manipuri dance form through institutions like the Manipuri Nartanalaya.

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, known for its graceful, fluid movements and themes drawn from Vaishnavite traditions, particularly the Ras Lila.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dance forms of India are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.

 

• The Jhaveri Sisters (Nayana, Suverna, Ranjana, and Darshana) are credited with popularising Manipuri dance across India from the mid-20th century onward.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 1): A classical dance-drama form of Kerala.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 2): A classical dance form of Tamil Nadu.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): A classical dance form associated with North India.

question: Which of the following trade agreements aims to ‘strengthen intra-SAARC economic cooperation to maximise the region's potential for trade and achieving development for their people'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SAFTA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• SAFTA (South Asian Free Trade Area) aims to promote and enhance mutual trade and economic cooperation among SAARC member states by reducing tariffs and other trade barriers. (सफ्टा — दक्षिण एशियाई मुक्त व्यापार क्षेत्र)

 

• It was signed at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad in January 2004 and came into force on 1 January 2006.

 

• Its objective is to maximise the region's potential for trade and development by promoting the free movement of goods among SAARC nations through the elimination of tariffs.

 

• Member states include India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was established in 1985, with its secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal.

 

• SAFTA succeeded the earlier SAPTA (South Asian Preferential Trade Agreement) of 1995.

 

NOTE

 

• APTA (Option 1): The Asia-Pacific Trade Agreement (formerly Bangkok Agreement) involves countries like India, China, South Korea, Bangladesh, Laos, and Sri Lanka — not specific to SAARC.

 

• NAFTA (Option 3): The North American Free Trade Agreement was between the USA, Canada, and Mexico (now replaced by USMCA).

 

• LAIA (Option 4): The Latin American Integration Association promotes trade among Latin American countries.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India enshrines to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51 (A).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A of the Constitution lists the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. (अनुच्छेद 51ए — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• Specifically, Article 51A(f) casts a duty on every citizen "to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture".

 

• Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IVA of the Constitution and are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

 

• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be directly enforced by courts, but they serve as a constant reminder of citizens' obligations to the nation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were added in 1976; an 11th duty (regarding parents providing education to children aged 6-14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• The Fundamental Duties are modelled on similar provisions and were introduced during the tenure of PM Indira Gandhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 43 (A) (Option 2): Deals with participation of workers in the management of industries.

 

• Article 48 (A) (Option 3): Directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife (a Directive Principle).

 

• Article 124 (A) (Option 4): Relates to the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC).

question: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda Dynasty of Magadha with the help of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishnugupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vishnugupta is another name for Chanakya (Kautilya), the astute strategist and author of the Arthashastra, who helped Chandragupta Maurya overthrow the Nanda dynasty of Magadha around 321 BCE. (विष्णुगुप्त — चाणक्य/कौटिल्य)

 

• Chanakya served as the chief advisor and mentor to Chandragupta Maurya, guiding the strategy that led to the establishment of the Mauryan Empire.

 

• The last Nanda ruler, Dhana Nanda, was defeated, and Chandragupta established his capital at Pataliputra.

 

• Chanakya's Arthashastra is a foundational treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy in ancient India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire (c. 321-297 BCE) and later, according to Jain tradition, abdicated the throne and became a Jain monk, migrating to Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.

 

• The Mauryan dynasty's most famous ruler was Ashoka, grandson of Chandragupta Maurya.

 

NOTE

 

• Skandagupta (Option 1): A ruler of the later Gupta Empire, known for repelling the Huna invasions.

 

• Chandragupta II (Option 2): A famous Gupta Empire ruler, also known as Vikramaditya, unrelated to the Mauryas.

 

• Samudragupta (Option 4): Another prominent Gupta Empire ruler, known as the "Napoleon of India".

question: In December 2021, who among the following became the first-ever Indian male shuttler to play in the final of the BWF World Championship Final?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kidambi Srikanth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kidambi Srikanth became the first Indian male shuttler to reach the final of the BWF World Championships, held in Huelva, Spain, in December 2021. (किदांबी श्रीकांत — बीडब्ल्यूएफ विश्व चैंपियनशिप)

 

• He won the silver medal after losing to Singapore's Loh Kean Yew in the final.

 

• This achievement marked a historic milestone for Indian men's badminton, as no Indian man had previously reached a World Championship singles final.

 

• The BWF World Championships is the sport's premier individual event, organised by the Badminton World Federation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• P.V. Sindhu is the most successful Indian at the BWF World Championships, having won a gold medal in 2019 and multiple other medals.

 

• B. Sai Praneeth won a bronze medal at the 2019 BWF World Championships.

 

NOTE

 

• B Sai Praneeth (Option 1): He won a bronze medal at the 2019 edition but did not reach a final.

 

• Chirag Shetty (Option 3): A doubles specialist, paired with Satwiksairaj Rankireddy; the pair reached the semi-final of the 2021 World Championships, not the final.

 

• V Diju (Option 4): A former Indian mixed doubles badminton player, not associated with this 2021 achievement.

question:
The sex ratio in various states and Union Territories is very important to get information about women in the country. Given below are statistics as per Census of India 2011. Match the following and identify the correct option.

States/UT: 1. Kerala  2. Puducherry  3. Delhi  4. Haryana

Females per 1000 males: a. 1037  b. 1084  c. 879  d. 868
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, the sex ratio (females per 1000 males) figures are: Kerala - 1084, Puducherry - 1037, Delhi - 868, Haryana - 879. (लिंगानुपात, जनगणना 2011 — केरल सर्वाधिक)

 

• Kerala (1084) has the highest sex ratio among all Indian states, matching code b.

 

• Puducherry (1037) among Union Territories has a relatively high sex ratio, matching code a.

 

• Delhi (868) matches code d, and Haryana (879), which has one of the lowest sex ratios among major states, matches code c.

 

• This gives the correct matching: 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The national average sex ratio as per Census 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males.

 

• Other UTs with notably high sex ratios include Lakshadweep; states with low sex ratios besides Haryana include Delhi and Chandigarh (a UT).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4: Each of these mismatches at least one state/UT with an incorrect sex-ratio figure, unlike the verified pairing in Option 2.

question: The All India Forward Bloc was founded by ________ in 1939 after resigning from the Congress Presidentship.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhash Chandra Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Subhash Chandra Bose founded the All India Forward Bloc in 1939 after resigning from the Indian National Congress presidency. (सुभाष चंद्र बोस — ऑल इंडिया फॉरवर्ड ब्लॉक)

 

• Bose had been elected INC President in 1938 and again in 1939 (defeating Gandhi's nominee, Pattabhi Sitaramayya), but resigned due to ideological differences with the Gandhian leadership over the approach to achieving independence.

 

• The Forward Bloc was formed as a left-wing nationalist political party within the Congress, advocating a more aggressive, militant approach to the freedom struggle.

 

• Bose later left India and formed the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) during World War II to fight for India's independence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subhash Chandra Bose is popularly known as "Netaji" and gave the famous slogan "Give me blood, and I will give you freedom".

 

• 23 January, his birth anniversary, is observed as Parakram Diwas in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Option 1): An early nationalist leader known for the slogan "Swaraj is my birthright", unrelated to the Forward Bloc.

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 2): Led the Congress's mainstream approach to independence, which Bose opposed on strategy.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 3): First Prime Minister of India, not the founder of the Forward Bloc.

question: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) - National Mission for Financial Inclusion completed how many years of implementation in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on 28 August 2014 and completed 8 years of implementation in 2022. (प्रधानमंत्री जन धन योजना — वित्तीय समावेशन)

 

• PMJDY is the National Mission for Financial Inclusion, aiming to ensure access to financial services such as banking/savings accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension for all households.

 

• It is administered by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.

 

• Under the scheme, beneficiaries get a RuPay debit card, accident insurance cover, and an overdraft facility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMJDY accounts do not require a minimum balance, making them accessible to economically weaker sections.

 

• As of its anniversaries, PMJDY has consistently been highlighted as one of the world's largest financial inclusion initiatives, with hundreds of millions of accounts opened.

 

NOTE

 

• 6, 9, 4 years (Options 1, 2, 4): These do not correctly reflect the gap between the 2014 launch and the year 2022.

question: Which of the following is also known as the ‘lender of the last resort'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is RBI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is known as the "lender of the last resort" because it provides financial assistance to commercial banks and financial institutions when they cannot obtain funds from any other source. (अंतिम ऋणदाता — भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक)

 

• This role helps maintain stability in the banking and financial system and prevents bank failures during liquidity crises.

 

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and is India's central bank.

 

• As the central bank, RBI also regulates monetary policy, issues currency, and supervises the banking sector.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI is headquartered in Mumbai; its central board is headed by the Governor of RBI.

 

• RBI was nationalised in 1949, a year after India's independence.

 

NOTE

 

• SEBI (Option 1): The Securities and Exchange Board of India regulates the securities market, not a lender of last resort.

 

• RRBs (Option 2): Regional Rural Banks provide banking services in rural areas; they are not lenders of last resort.

 

• SBI (Option 4): The State Bank of India is India's largest commercial bank, not the central bank.

question: Which of the following group elements are called chalcogens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Group-16.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The elements of Group 16 of the periodic table are known as chalcogens, also called the oxygen family. (चाल्कोजन — समूह 16)

 

• This group includes Oxygen (O), Sulphur (S), Selenium (Se), Tellurium (Te), and Polonium (Po).

 

• The term "chalcogen" is derived from Greek words meaning "ore-forming", as many metal ores contain sulfides, oxides, or other chalcogen compounds.

 

• These elements have six electrons in their outermost shell and commonly form compounds with a -2 oxidation state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Oxygen, the most abundant element in the Earth's crust after silicon, is the lightest chalcogen and essential for respiration.

 

• Group 17 elements are called halogens, and Group 18 elements are called noble gases.

 

NOTE

 

• Group-2 (Option 2): Known as alkaline earth metals (e.g., Beryllium, Magnesium, Calcium).

 

• Group-17 (Option 3): Known as halogens (e.g., Fluorine, Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine).

 

• Group-18 (Option 4): Known as noble gases (e.g., Helium, Neon, Argon).

question: Which of the following acids makes up 55–80% of olive oil, making it a good choice for most cooking methods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oleic acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Oleic acid, a monounsaturated fatty acid, makes up approximately 55-83% of olive oil, making it its predominant fatty acid. (ओलिक एसिड — जैतून का तेल)

 

• Because monounsaturated fats are relatively stable at higher temperatures compared to polyunsaturated fats, olive oil (rich in oleic acid) is considered a good choice for most cooking methods, including sautéing and roasting.

 

• Oleic acid is also associated with several health benefits, including supporting heart health by helping to reduce LDL ("bad") cholesterol levels.

 

• Olive oil is a key component of the Mediterranean diet, widely studied for its cardiovascular benefits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Extra virgin olive oil is the least processed form of olive oil, retaining the highest levels of antioxidants and nutrients.

 

• Other oils rich in oleic acid include canola oil and avocado oil.

 

NOTE

 

• Lauric acid (Option 1): A saturated fatty acid predominantly found in coconut oil and palm kernel oil.

 

• Arachidic acid (Option 3): A saturated fatty acid found in small amounts in peanut oil.

 

• Stearic acid (Option 4): A saturated fatty acid found in animal fats and cocoa butter, present only in small amounts in olive oil.

question: What is an instrument that sends pulses of electromagnetic energy into the atmosphere to detect rainfall, determine its speed and intensity, and identify precipitation types such as rain, snow or hail?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Doppler weather radar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Doppler weather radar sends out pulses of electromagnetic energy (microwaves) into the atmosphere; these pulses reflect off precipitation particles, allowing the radar to detect rainfall, determine its speed and intensity, and identify the type of precipitation (rain, snow, or hail). (डॉपलर मौसम रडार — वर्षा का पता लगाना)

 

• It uses the Doppler effect — the change in frequency of the reflected waves — to measure the velocity of precipitation particles moving toward or away from the radar, which helps in detecting storm systems and wind patterns.

 

• Doppler weather radars are extensively used by meteorological departments (such as the India Meteorological Department, IMD) for short-term weather forecasting and cyclone tracking.

 

• This technology is crucial for issuing timely warnings about severe weather events like thunderstorms, hailstorms, and cyclones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IMD operates a network of Doppler Weather Radars (DWRs) across India to monitor cyclones and severe weather.

 

• Doppler radar technology is also used in aviation for detecting wind shear and turbulence.

 

NOTE

 

• Barometer (Option 1): Measures atmospheric pressure, not precipitation.

 

• Spectral pyranometer (Option 2): Measures solar radiation (broadband or spectral irradiance), not rainfall.

 

• 2D sonic anemometer (Option 3): Measures wind speed and direction using ultrasonic signals, not precipitation.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Parliamentary Committees?

A. A minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee.

B. The members of the Estimates Committee are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

C. A minister can be a member of the Estimates Committee if he is nominated by the Speaker.

D. A member of the Committee on Public Undertakings will have tenure of 2 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Statement A is correct: a minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC); if an existing member is subsequently appointed a minister, they cease to be a member of the Committee from the date of that appointment. (लोक लेखा समिति — मंत्री सदस्य नहीं हो सकता)

 

• Statement B is incorrect: Members of the Estimates Committee are elected by the Lok Sabha every year from amongst its own members (by proportional representation via single transferable vote); they are not nominated by the Speaker.

 

• Statement C is incorrect: A minister cannot be a member of the Estimates Committee at all, regardless of Speaker's nomination — the same restriction that applies to the PAC applies here.

 

• Statement D is incorrect: A member of the Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) has a tenure of one year, not two years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee, and Committee on Public Undertakings are the three key Financial Committees of Parliament.

 

• The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha only; the PAC and COPU draw members from both Houses.

 

NOTE

 

• A, B and C only (Option 2): Incorrectly includes B and C, which misstate the selection process and minister eligibility for the Estimates Committee.

 

• A, B, C and D (Option 3): Incorrectly includes all of B, C and D, which are all factually wrong.

 

• B, C and D only (Option 4): Incorrectly includes only the false statements while excluding the one correct statement, A.

question: The famous Arabic scholar Al Biruni came to contact with India through _________ in the eleventh century A.D.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahmud Ghaznavi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Al-Biruni, the famous Persian/Arabic-writing polymath, came into contact with India in the 11th century A.D. through Mahmud of Ghazni (Ghaznavi), whose court he was attached to and whose invasions of India he accompanied. (अल-बिरूनी — महमूद गजनवी)

 

• During his time in India, Al-Biruni studied Sanskrit, Indian philosophy, mathematics, astronomy, and customs, producing the celebrated work "Kitab-ul-Hind" (Tahqiq-i-Hind).

 

• His writings are considered one of the most valuable and objective accounts of Indian society and science in the medieval period.

 

• Mahmud Ghaznavi ruled the Ghaznavid Empire and led numerous raids into the Indian subcontinent between 1000-1027 A.D., notably the raid on the Somnath temple.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Al-Biruni is also credited with early estimations of the Earth's radius and contributions to geography, mathematics, and comparative religion.

 

• Mahmud Ghaznavi's court was also home to the poet Firdausi, author of the Shahnama.

 

NOTE

 

• Abdullah Shah Ghazi (Option 1): A Sufi saint associated with Sindh (Karachi), unrelated to Al-Biruni's arrival in India.

 

• Al-Walid I (Option 3): An Umayyad Caliph under whom Muhammad Bin Qasim invaded Sindh in 712 A.D., centuries before Al-Biruni.

 

• Muhammad Bin Qasim (Option 4): Led the Arab conquest of Sindh in 712 A.D., unrelated to Al-Biruni, who arrived three centuries later.

question: When did the All India Congress formalise the demand for ‘Purna Swaraj' or full independence for India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is At its Lahore Session in 1929.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National Congress formally adopted the goal of "Purna Swaraj" (complete independence) at its Lahore Session in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. (पूर्ण स्वराज — लाहौर अधिवेशन, 1929)

 

• It was resolved that 26 January 1930 would be observed as "Purna Swaraj Day" (Independence Day) across the country, with the tricolour flag hoisted and pledges taken.

 

• This session marked a turning point, shifting the Congress's demand from "Dominion Status" to complete independence from British rule.

 

• The resolution set the stage for the subsequent Civil Disobedience Movement, launched by Gandhi with the Dandi March in 1930.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 26 January continues to be celebrated as Republic Day in independent India, in memory of this pledge.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru became the youngest Congress President at the Lahore session (at the time), succeeding Motilal Nehru.

 

NOTE

 

• Karachi Session (Option 1), 1931: Notable for the resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy, presided over by Sardar Patel, held after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

 

• Guwahati Session (Option 3), 1926: Presided over by S. Srinivasa Iyengar; not associated with the Purna Swaraj declaration.

 

• Madras Session (Option 4), 1927: First to pass a resolution on complete independence as a goal (moved by Jawaharlal Nehru), but it was formally adopted as official Congress policy only at Lahore in 1929.

question: ‘A Plan of Economic Development for India' is also known as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "A Plan of Economic Development for India", published in 1944-45, is popularly known as the Bombay Plan. (बॉम्बे प्लान — 1944)

 

• It was drafted by eight leading Indian industrialists, including J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla, Purshottamdas Thakurdas, and Ardeshir Dalal, envisioning a mixed economy with substantial state intervention for post-independence economic development.

 

• The plan proposed doubling per capita income and significantly expanding industrial and agricultural output within 15 years, with heavy reliance on state planning.

 

• Though never officially implemented, the Bombay Plan influenced India's subsequent Five-Year Plans and the adoption of a mixed economy model after independence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other economic plans of the pre-independence era include the Gandhian Plan (1944) by Shriman Narayan and the People's Plan (1945) by M.N. Roy.

 

• India's first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951 under the Planning Commission, chaired by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi Plan, Gujarat Plan, Surat Plan (Options 1, 2, 3): These are not recognised historical titles for this document; the plan is exclusively known as the Bombay Plan, reflecting the city where its authors were based.

question: For the year 2022, who among the following won the Indian Film Personality Award awarded by International Film Festival of India (IFFI)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chiranjeevi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Telugu megastar Chiranjeevi was honoured with the "Indian Film Personality of the Year" award at the 53rd International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2022, held in Goa. (चिरंजीवी — भारतीय फिल्म व्यक्तित्व पुरस्कार 2022)

 

• The award recognised his decades-long contribution to Indian cinema, spanning acting, production, and philanthropy.

 

• IFFI is one of Asia's oldest and most significant international film festivals, organised annually by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India.

 

• The award was presented at the closing ceremony of the festival in November 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 53rd IFFI (2022) also featured Sylvester Stallone, honoured with the IFFI Icon of the Golden Jubilee Award.

 

• Past recipients of the Indian Film Personality of the Year award include Rajinikanth (2019) and Biswajit Chatterjee (2021).

 

NOTE

 

• Prakash Raj (Option 2), Mahesh Babu (Option 3), Rajnikant (Option 4): None of these actors received the Indian Film Personality of the Year award for 2022; Rajinikanth had won it earlier, in 2019.

question: In the 15th century, a text called _________ is ascribed popularly to Lochan Kavi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raag Tarangini.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 15th century musicological text "Raga Tarangini" (Ragatarangini) is popularly ascribed to Lochan Kavi (Lochana Pandita). (राग तरंगिणी — लोचन कवि)

 

• The text is an important treatise in the history of Hindustani classical music, discussing the classification of ragas.

 

• Lochana Pandita's work is notable for introducing a "mela" (parent scale) system of raga classification, which was later carried forward by other music theorists.

 

• It represents one of the significant medieval Sanskrit works on Indian music theory, contributing to the evolution of raga classification systems used even today.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The "Sangeet Darpan" is an important treatise by Damodara Mishra, dealing with Hindustani classical music.

 

• The "mela" system of raga classification was later refined by Venkatamakhin in his work "Chaturdandi Prakashika" (17th century) for Carnatic music.

 

NOTE

 

• Hridayaprakash (Option 1): Not the popularly recognised title for Lochan Kavi's 15th-century text.

 

• Sangeet Darpan (Option 2): Authored by Damodara Mishra, a different musicological text.

 

• Anup Vilas (Option 3): Not associated with Lochan Kavi; it is not the standard title for this text.

question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding the liver?
option_1: It is situated in the upper part of the abdomen on the left side.
option_2: It secretes bile juice that is stored in a sac called the gall bladder.
option_3: It is the largest gland in the body.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is situated in the upper part of the abdomen on the left side.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This statement is incorrect because the liver is situated in the upper right side of the abdomen, beneath the diaphragm, not the left side. (यकृत — उदर के दाहिने ऊपरी भाग में स्थित)

 

• The liver is the largest internal organ and the largest gland in the human body, weighing approximately 1.5 kg in adults.

 

• It is a reddish-brown coloured organ, divided into a larger right lobe and a smaller left lobe.

 

• The liver secretes bile, a digestive fluid that helps in the digestion and absorption of fats; the bile is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder, a small sac located beneath the liver.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The liver performs numerous vital functions including detoxification, protein synthesis (e.g., albumin, clotting factors), glycogen storage, and metabolism of drugs and nutrients.

 

• The liver has a remarkable capacity for regeneration, able to regrow even after partial removal (e.g., in living-donor liver transplants).

 

NOTE

 

• It secretes bile juice stored in the gall bladder (Option 2): This is a correct statement about the liver, hence not the answer.

 

• It is the largest gland in the body (Option 3): This is a correct statement, as the liver is indeed the body's largest gland.

 

• It is a reddish-brown gland (Option 4): This is also a correct, factual description of the liver.

question: During which of the following periods was the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup held in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11-30 October.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 was hosted by India and held from 11 to 30 October 2022. (फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप — भारत, अक्टूबर 2022)

 

• Matches were played across three venues: Bhubaneswar, Navi Mumbai, and Goa.

 

• The tournament was won by Spain, who defeated Colombia in the final.

 

• This was the first FIFA tournament of any kind to be hosted by India at the U-17 women's level, following India's earlier hosting of the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup in 2017.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's team was eliminated in the group stage, but the tournament was notable for record-breaking attendance figures for a women's youth football event.

 

• The tournament mascot was named "Ibha", a female clouded leopard.

 

NOTE

 

• 4-11 April, 8-21 June, 11-19 December (Options 2, 3, 4): These date ranges do not correspond to the actual FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022, which was held in October 2022.

question: Whose research was fundamental in establishing the modern discipline known as surface tension,Which describes the properties of liquid and solid surfaces and interfaces?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agnes Pockels.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Agnes Pockels, a self-taught German scientist, is credited with pioneering research fundamental to establishing the modern discipline of surface tension and surface chemistry. (एग्नेस पोकल्स — पृष्ठ तनाव)

 

• Despite lacking formal scientific training or access to a laboratory (due to the social restrictions on women in science at the time), she conducted careful kitchen-sink experiments and developed a simple device (the "Pockels trough") to measure surface tension.

 

• Her findings, published with the help of physicist Lord Rayleigh in the journal Nature (1891), laid the groundwork for the study of thin films and monolayers at liquid surfaces.

 

• Her work significantly influenced later developments in surface chemistry, including the studies of Irving Langmuir, who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1932 for related work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The "Pockels trough" she designed was a precursor to the modern Langmuir-Blodgett trough, still used in surface science today.

 

• Agnes Pockels received an honorary doctorate from the Braunschweig University of Technology in 1932 in recognition of her contributions.

 

NOTE

 

• Gerty Cori (Option 1): Won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (1947) for work on carbohydrate metabolism (the Cori cycle).

 

• Nettie Stevens (Option 2): A geneticist known for discovering the role of the X and Y chromosomes in sex determination.

 

• Lise Meitner (Option 3): A physicist known for her contribution to the discovery of nuclear fission.

question: Where does the Narmada river rise?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amarkantak Ranges.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Narmada river rises from the Amarkantak Plateau/Ranges in Anuppur district, Madhya Pradesh, at an elevation of about 1,057 metres. (नर्मदा नदी — अमरकंटक)

 

• It flows westward for about 1,312 km through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat before draining into the Arabian Sea via the Gulf of Khambhat.

 

• The Narmada is one of the few major Indian rivers that flows in a rift valley, running east to west between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

 

• It is often referred to as the "Life Line of Madhya Pradesh" and holds great religious significance, with the parikrama (circumambulation) of the river being an important pilgrimage tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The famous Marble Rocks are located at Bhedaghat, near Jabalpur, along the Narmada's course.

 

• Other major rivers rising from the Amarkantak region include the Son River, which flows eastward, in contrast to the westward-flowing Narmada.

 

NOTE

 

• Western Ghats (Option 1): Source of peninsular rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri, not the Narmada.

 

• Gawilgarh Hills (Option 2): A range within the Satpura hill system in Maharashtra, not the source of the Narmada.

 

• Satpura Ranges (Option 3): The Narmada flows along the Satpura range (which forms its southern boundary) but does not originate from it; its true source is the Amarkantak plateau.
